customManagers.description: Runner image Go toolchain; must equal apps/runner-autoscaler/go.mod's go directive (toolchain-health.test.sh)
Runner image Corepack: Node 25+ stopped bundling it, so the image installs this npm release before resolving pnpm from packageManager.

Node runtime copies outside a FROM line: the assertions that the Node binary copied out of the pinned node base image is the expected release, the runner image's NodeSource apt pin, and setup-node-pnpm's default (which must equal the runner image's baked Node for detect-baked.sh to reuse it). They must equal the node base image tag (tools/contract-tests/node-version-pins.test.ts); #3092 moved only the FROM lines and every runner-image publication failed at control-plane-verify-runtime.

Console production runtime base. Distroless publishes one floating image per Node major, so Renovate moves only the nonroot tag's digest; the major in the image name must equal the node base image's (tools/contract-tests/node-version-pins.test.ts). #3104 moved every other pin to Node 26 and the console kept running 24.22.1 here.

packageRules.description: @types/node must track the Node major the repo runs on (engines `<27`, CI/runner image/deploy pinned to 26.x), not the newest Node: a newer major types APIs the runtime lacks, so typecheck would pass code that fails in production. Move it together with the Node pins in a deliberate runtime upgrade (#3101 closed #3053 for this reason).

pnpm majors change install/lockfile semantics for the whole workspace at once (packageManager pins the exact version, currently 11.x); hold them for a deliberate toolchain upgrade rather than a bot PR

pnpm 11.28.3 creates self-referential links for skipped platform-specific optional dependencies on Linux, which makes Next/Turbopack standalone tracing fail; allow later 11.x fixes while holding only the broken release

The runner image's curated pnpm-store seed and its regression fixtures are refreshed deliberately (pnpm-seed/README.md: no more than monthly, independent of consumer dependency updates), and the image only ever reads their lockfiles (`pnpm fetch --frozen-lockfile`). Renovate bumped the fixture package.json files weekly without touching those locks, so the manifests drifted from what is actually seeded, the fixtures made up about half of the weekly group, and the still-locked vitest 4.1.11 kept a phantom 'update vitest monorepo to v5' major on the dashboard (#3) after the repo itself had moved to vitest 5. pnpm is NOT exempt: each fleet seed's packageManager is copied from its source repository by tools/sync-runner-pnpm-seed.py, and when #2084 bumped it here Renovate re-ran pnpm against the seed's dependency-less package.json and rewrote all four fleet lockfiles to empty, which failed every runner-image build (merge-to-live) until they were restored.

CI's JDK deliberately tracks a floating Temurin major line ('21'), like node '24' and actions/setup-java v6. The java-version datasource can only offer exact builds (re-bumped every quarter) or a new major (25), and the JVM here only runs the Firestore emulator: the runner image installs openjdk-21-jre-headless and the E2E sandbox image Ubuntu Noble's default-jre-headless (Java 21), so moving setup-java alone would split the fleet across two JVMs for no benefit. Same rule and reasoning as sprinkles. Revisit when the sandbox base image's default JRE moves (#2001).

oRPC is exact-pinned on the v2 beta line and sits on the console's server-function boundary, where unit tests and typecheck miss breakage. Upgrade it by deliberate PR, as sprinkles does, not inside the auto-merged weekly group (#1971's beta bump changed the generated OpenAPI document and failed Verify). Disabling lookups also removes the dashboard's standing '@orpc/next deprecated' row, which is npm's flag on the mistaken 1.14.11 publish, not on the beta line in use.

The tools/e2e/Dockerfile mcr.microsoft.com/playwright tag must match the resolved @playwright/test version (tools/contract-tests/baked-ci-tools.test.ts), so they move in one group. The image has no release timestamp, so it is proposed immediately while the npm package waits out its 1-day release age; minimumGroupSize 2 holds the branch until both are ready instead of opening a tag-only PR that fails CI (#2170). Same rule as sprinkles' playwright group.

A republished Playwright image (same tag, new digest) has no npm counterpart to group with, so exempt digest-only updates from the playwright group's minimumGroupSize; Renovate applies the highest minimumGroupSize in a branch, so a version bump still waits for both.

The runner image's Go toolchain (ARG GO_VERSION) and apps/runner-autoscaler/go.mod's go directive move together: runner-image/toolchain-health.test.sh fails CI when they differ. The dockerfile manager resolves golang:${GO_VERSION}-bookworm through the ARG and keeps proposing a -bookworm tag, but its replace string never occurs in the file, so every grouped PR (#2907, #2917, #2920) listed the bump without changing the Dockerfile and the dashboard kept it pending. Read the ARG through the customManagers entry instead, and let the go directive bump (go-mod-directive versioning treats it as a range, so without rangeStrategy bump it is never proposed), so both land in one grouped PR.
Bump apps/runner-autoscaler/go.mod's go directive together with the runner image's ARG GO_VERSION (see the rule above).

Every Node pin moves in one PR: the node base images (dockerfile manager), the copies the Node customManagers entry reads, and package.json engines (node-version datasource). Separate PRs (#3092 images, #3093 deploy-console) let the base image move without its runtime assertions; node-version-pins.test.ts now fails any PR that leaves a copy behind.

actions/setup-node's node-version is reported as depName node on the github-releases datasource (actions/node-versions), so the rule above cannot match it; join the same group so deploy workflows move with the images.

The runner image installs Node from NodeSource (ARG NODE_VERSION), which publishes well after nodejs.org: measured from the node-version datasource's day-granular release date, 24.22.1 (2026-10-20) reached NodeSource at 2026-10-21 16:17Z and 24.22.2 (2026-10-27) at 2026-10-28 19:07Z, about 43 hours. Hold the node-version datasource three days so the group never merges a release NodeSource has not published; the docker FROM bump arrives first and node-version-pins.test.ts keeps the group PR red until the copies catch up.
